literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengcheng and held the post of Qiaozhou inspector.
idiomatic: In Liang he was Marquis of Fengcheng and Qiaozhou inspector.

literal: Hou Jing attacked and took it; he was captured, then soon fled to Jiangling.
idiomatic: Hou Jing seized him; he escaped to Jiangling.

literal: Liang Emperor Yuan pacified Hou Jing.
idiomatic: Liang Yuan Di pacified Hou Jing.

literal: Tai was made concurrent Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Interior Minister of Guiyang.
idiomatic: Tai was made concurrent grand master of splendid happiness and interior minister of Guiyang.

literal: Before he reached the commandery, Yu Jin took Jiangling; he then followed his elder brother Xiu to assist at Yingzhou.
idiomatic: Before he took office, Yu Jin took Jiangling; he followed his brother Xiu to Yingzhou.

literal: When Xiu died, Tai was at once made inspector.
idiomatic: When Xiu died, Tai became inspector.

literal: Xiangzhou Inspector Wang Lin attacked Tai; Tai surrendered the province to Lin.
idiomatic: Xiangzhou inspector Wang Lin attacked; Tai surrendered the province.

literal: At the time Chen Emperor Wu held power and summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary, but he did not accept.
idiomatic: Chen Wu summoned him as attendant-in-ordinary; he refused.

literal: He then fled to Qi and was Yongzhou inspector.
idiomatic: He fled to Qi as Yongzhou inspector.

literal: In the fourth year of Baoding, Grand General Quan Jingxuan seized territory in Henan; Tai then returned to Western Wei.
idiomatic: Baoding 4, Quan Jingxuan seized Henan; Tai returned to Western Wei.

literal: Because his name violated Zhou Emperor Wen's taboo, he was addressed by his style.
idiomatic: His name tabooed Zhou Wen Di; he was called by his style.

literal: He was appointed Commissioner with the Grand Insignia, Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, enfeoffed Duke of Yixing commandery, and made Cai prefecture inspector.
idiomatic: He was commissioner equal to the three dukes, duke of Yixing, and Cai inspector.

literal: His government preserved simplicity and kindness and deeply reassured officials and people.
idiomatic: His rule was simple and kind; officials and people were at ease.

literal: He died in office; son Bao inherited.
idiomatic: He died in office; son Bao inherited.

literal: Bao, styled Jizhen, had fine bearing and was skilled at witty talk; before the capping age his name weighed on the age.
idiomatic: Bao, styled Jizhen, was handsome and witty; before capping age he was famed.

literal: When Sui Emperor Wen aided the government, he was drawn as chief clerk of the chancellor's office.
idiomatic: When Sui Wen Di aided the government, he was chief clerk of the chancellor's office.

literal: In the Kaihuang era he rose to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: In Kaihuang he rose to vice minister of personnel.

literal: Later he was executed for the affair of Crown Prince Yong; people of the time thought it unjust.
idiomatic: Later he was executed in Crown Prince Yong's affair; the age thought it unjust.

literal: Xiao Hui, styled Zhiyao, was son of Liang Emperor Wu's younger brother Prince Ancheng Xiu.
idiomatic: Xiao Hui, styled Zhiyao, was son of Liang Wu Di's brother Prince Ancheng Xiu.

literal: His nature was mild and generous, with dignified bearing; in Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongfeng county.
idiomatic: Mild and generous, with dignified bearing; in Liang he was Marquis of Yongfeng.

literal: Eastern Wei sent Li Xie and Lu Yuanming as envoys to Liang.
idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Li Xie and Lu Yuanming to Liang.

literal: Liang Emperor Wu, finding Hui's eloquence admirable, had him concurrently serve as vice director of the Secretariat and receive tribute at the guest lodge.
idiomatic: Liang Wu Di admired his eloquence and had him receive envoys as vice director of the secretariat.

literal: He passed through vice director of the Yellow Gate and rose in succession to prefect of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.
idiomatic: He was vice director of the yellow gate and rose to Baxi and Zitong prefect.

literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Prince Wuling Ji assumed the imperial title.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Prince Wuling Ji took the throne.

literal: Of the imperial clan in Shu at the time only Hui remained; Ji enfeoffed Hui Prince of Qin commandery.
idiomatic: Only Hui of the clan remained in Shu; Ji made him Prince of Qin.

literal: Ji led his host east; he made Hui Secretariat Director, Grand General Who Pacifies the West, area commander, and Yizhou inspector, to hold Chengdu.
idiomatic: Ji marched east, made Hui secretariat director, grand general who pacifies the west, area commander, and Yizhou inspector at Chengdu.

literal: He also ordered Liangzhou Inspector Yang Qianyun to hold Tong prefecture.
idiomatic: He ordered Liangzhou inspector Yang Qianyun to hold Tong prefecture.

literal: Zhou Emperor Wen knew Shu troops were few and weak and sent Grand General Yuchi Jiong to command the host against them.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen Di sent grand general Yuchi Jiong against the weak Shu host.

literal: Jiong entered Jian'ge and drove straight to Chengdu.
idiomatic: Jiong entered Jian'ge and drove to Chengdu.

literal: Hui saw troops under ten thousand and storehouses empty; he then led civil and military officials north of Yizhou city, together with Jiong ascended the altar, drank blood, and made alliance, surrendering the city to Wei.
idiomatic: With under ten thousand troops and empty stores, he led officials north of the city, swore alliance with Jiong, and surrendered to Wei.

literal: He was appointed attendant-in-ordinary and commissioner equal to the three dukes, enfeoffed Duke of Guishan county.
idiomatic: He was attendant-in-ordinary, commissioner equal to the three dukes, and duke of Guishan.

literal: When Zhou Emperor Min succeeded, his rank rose to Duke of Huangtai commandery.
idiomatic: When Zhou Min Di succeeded, he became duke of Huangtai.

literal: In the Wucheng era, Emperor Ming ordered literary Confucians at Qilin Hall to collate the classics and histories and also compile the Genealogies of the Age; Hui also took part.
idiomatic: In Wucheng, Ming Di had scholars collate classics at Qilin Hall and compile genealogies; Hui took part.

literal: Soon, because his mother was old and he also had illness, he requested to write books outside court; an edict permitted it.
idiomatic: His mother was old and he was ill; he asked to write outside court and was permitted.

literal: In the first year of Baoding he was made Grand Master of Rites in the Ministry of Rites; for merit in returning and submitting he was separately granted five hundred households of Duoling county to collect rents.
idiomatic: Baoding 1 he was grand master of rites; for returning merit he received five hundred households' rent at Duoling.

literal: In the third year he went out as Shang prefecture inspector.
idiomatic: In the third year he was Shang prefecture inspector.

literal: His government took ritual yielding as its root; once on New Year's Day he released all prisoners in the jail to return home and allowed three days before they must return to prison.
idiomatic: He governed by courtesy; on New Year's he sent all prisoners home for three days.

literal: The chief officer disputed it; Hui said: "In former histories Wang Chang and Yu Yan were praised.
idiomatic: The jailer objected; Hui said, "Wang Chang and Yu Yan were praised in history.

literal: Though my virtue is slight, I secretly cherish their lofty conduct.
idiomatic: My virtue is slight, but I cherish their example.

literal: To be punished for this I would be all the more willing.
idiomatic: Punishment for this I would gladly accept.

literal: "The prisoners received his grace and all returned within the limit; officials and people praised his benevolent transformation.
idiomatic: Prisoners returned on time; officials and people praised his kindness.

literal: When his term ended and he was about to return, more than three hundred people of the department, Ji Qi and others, submitted a memorial asking that he stay two more years.
idiomatic: As his term ended, over three hundred led by Ji Qi asked him to stay two more years.

literal: Though the edict did not permit it, the court greatly praised the beauty of it.
idiomatic: The edict refused, but the court greatly praised it.

literal: When Hui entered court it happened that Lumen school was established.
idiomatic: When Hui came to court, Lumen school was established.

literal: Emperor Wu made Hui, with Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, Wang Bao, and three others, all literary erudites.
idiomatic: Wu Di made Hui, Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, Wang Bao, and three others literary erudites.

literal: Hui, because his mother was old, memorialized asking to return and nourish her in private; the emperor did not permit it.
idiomatic: He asked to nurse his mother at home; the emperor refused.

literal: Soon he left office on his mother's mourning.
idiomatic: Soon he left office for his mother's mourning.

literal: He passed through junior guardian and junior tutor and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Caiyang commandery.
idiomatic: He was junior guardian and junior tutor and became duke of Caiyang.

literal: At his death Emperor Wu mourned at Zhengwu Hall and posthumously gave him bearer of the staff, grand general, area commander, junior tutor, and Yizhou inspector, with posthumous name Xiang.
idiomatic: At his death Wu Di mourned at Zhengwu Hall and gave him grand general, junior tutor, Yizhou inspector, posthumous name Xiang.

literal: Hui was skilled at cursive and clerical script; his calligraphic name was second to Wang Bao's; he also took note of arithmetic and medical recipes.
idiomatic: He excelled at cursive and clerical script, second to Wang Bao, and knew arithmetic and medicine.

literal: Works of poetry, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous prose in tens of thousands of words circulated in the world.
idiomatic: Tens of thousands of words of poetry and prose circulated.

literal: Son Ji, styled Decheng, from youth was humane and generous and rather loved composing prose.
idiomatic: Son Ji, styled Decheng, was humane and loved prose.

literal: He was Eastern Central Commander of Gentlemen and followed Hui to court.
idiomatic: He was eastern central commander and followed Hui to court.

literal: When Zhou Emperor Xiao Min succeeded, he was made recorder of the inner and outer offices and later rose to prefect of Boyang commandery.
idiomatic: When Xiao Min Di succeeded, he was recorder of the inner and outer offices and later Boyang prefect.

literal: Xiao Yuansu, styled Minggong, was grandson of Liang Emperor Wu and son of Prince Wuling Ji.
idiomatic: Xiao Yuansu, styled Minggong, was Liang Wu Di's grandson and Prince Wuling Ji's son.

literal: His bearing was refined and elegant; he was quick and loved learning.
idiomatic: Refined bearing; quick and studious.

literal: When Ji assumed the imperial title, Yuansu was enfeoffed Prince of Yidu and made attendant-in-ordinary.
idiomatic: When Ji took the throne, Yuansu was Prince of Yidu and attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: When Ji went down the gorges he ordered Yuansu to assist Xiao Hui in holding Chengdu.
idiomatic: Ji went down the gorges and left Yuansu to assist Hui at Chengdu.

literal: When Yuchi Jiong arrived, he and Hui both surrendered.
idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong arrived, he and Hui surrendered.

literal: He was appointed commissioner equal to the three dukes and attendant-in-ordinary, enfeoffed Duke of Anhua county.
idiomatic: He was commissioner equal to the three dukes, attendant-in-ordinary, and duke of Anhua.

literal: At the beginning of Zhou Emperor Ming's reign he was advanced to Duke of Jicheng commandery for merit in returning and submitting.
idiomatic: At Ming Di's accession he became duke of Jicheng for returning merit.

literal: He was separately granted five hundred households of Sijun county to collect rents.
idiomatic: He received five hundred households' rent at Sijun.

literal: Later he was made Xianyang commandery prefect and had very fine administrative achievements.
idiomatic: Later he was Xianyang prefect with fine achievements.

literal: Soon he was reassigned junior tutor of the crown prince and wrote the Admonition of the Junior Tutor.
idiomatic: Soon he was crown prince junior tutor and wrote the Admonition of the Junior Tutor.

literal: The crown prince saw it and was pleased and sent a letter of thanks and inquiry.
idiomatic: The crown prince was pleased and sent thanks.

literal: He was reassigned Feng prefecture inspector, soon advanced to commissioner with the grand insignia equal in rank to the grand general, passed through grand master of the lineage in the Ministry of Rites and Luozhou inspector, and advanced to grand general.
idiomatic: He was Feng inspector, then commissioner equal to the grand general, lineage grand master, Luozhou inspector, and grand general.

literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was made Beizhou inspector; because his mother was old he asked to return and nourish her and was permitted; he died at home.
idiomatic: At Sui Kaihuang he was Beizhou inspector, asked to nurse his mother, was permitted, and died at home.

literal: He had a collected works in ten scrolls; he also compiled contemporaries' poetry and brushwork into Literary Sea in forty scrolls, Broad Mirror in ten scrolls, and Records of Huaihai in Turmoil in four scrolls, all circulating in the world.
idiomatic: He had collected works in ten scrolls and compiled Literary Sea, Broad Mirror, and Records of Huaihai in Turmoil, all circulating.

literal: At the time Dahuan's elder brother Prince of Runan Dafeng and others had still not presented court audience.
idiomatic: Dahuan's brother Prince of Runan Dafeng had not yet presented audience.

literal: Yuan Di's nature was jealous and harsh; he greatly resented them and therefore sent Dahuan to summon them.
idiomatic: Yuan Di was jealous and resentful and sent Dahuan to summon them.

literal: Dahuan that same day instructed them clearly; the two elder brothers in succession went out to audience and Yuan Di was then at ease.
idiomatic: Dahuan instructed them; both brothers presented audience and Yuan Di was reassured.

literal: Dahuan feared slander might brew and therefore cut off human affairs;
idiomatic: Fearing slander, Dahuan cut off worldly affairs;

literal: retainers left and right were no more than two or three.
idiomatic: he kept only two or three retainers.

literal: He did not roam or play idly; between elder brothers and sisters he used only letters.
idiomatic: He did not roam idly; with siblings he wrote only letters.

literal: He constantly took reading the Odes, Rites, Documents, and Changes as his occupation.
idiomatic: He constantly read the Odes, Rites, Documents, and Changes.

literal: Yuan Di once himself asked several dozen main points of the Five Classics; Dahuan's words were concise and pointed, his answers without hesitation.
idiomatic: Yuan Di asked dozens of points on the Five Classics; Dahuan answered concisely without pause.

literal: The emperor greatly sighed in admiration and said: "In former times Prince Hejian loved learning—you already have that;
idiomatic: The emperor praised him: "Prince Hejian loved learning—you have that;

literal: Prince Linzi loved literature—you also combine that.
idiomatic: Prince Linzi loved literature—you combine that too.

literal: Yet in doing good like Prince Dongping you surpass the former records."
idiomatic: Yet in doing good like Prince Dongping you surpass old examples."

literal: When Yu Jin's army arrived, Yuan Di ordered Dafeng to serve as envoy seeking peace and Dahuan as deputy—in truth they were hostages.
idiomatic: When Yu Jin arrived, Yuan Di sent Dafeng to sue for peace and Dahuan as deputy—in truth hostages.

literal: They went out to the army camp; after two nights Yuan Di surrendered.
idiomatic: At the army camp, after two nights Yuan Di surrendered.

literal: In the second year of Wei Emperor Gong, Dahuan reached Chang'an; Zhou Emperor Wen received him with guest rites.
idiomatic: Wei Gong Di 2, Dahuan reached Chang'an; Zhou Wen Di received him as a guest.

literal: In the second year of Baoding, Dafeng was Duke of Jinling county and Dahuan Duke of Shining county.
idiomatic: Baoding 2, Dafeng was duke of Jinling and Dahuan duke of Shining.

literal: Soon Dahuan was further made Grand General of Cavalry and Chariots and commissioner equal to the three dukes.
idiomatic: Soon Dahuan was grand general of cavalry and chariots, commissioner equal to the three dukes.

literal: Shortly after, Qilin Hall was opened and scholars gathered; Dahuan took part.
idiomatic: Qilin Hall opened and gathered scholars; Dahuan took part.

literal: Collected Works of Liang Emperor Wu in forty scrolls and Brief Collected Works in ninety scrolls each existed in only one copy; after Jiangling was pacified they were both stored in the secret archive.
idiomatic: Liang Wu Di's collected works and brief collected works existed in single copies stored in the secret archive after Jiangling fell.

literal: When Dahuan entered Qilin he first saw them and thereupon copied both collections by hand, finishing both in one year; those who knew praised and marveled.
idiomatic: Entering Qilin he copied both collections by hand in one year; observers marveled.

literal: Dahuan deeply believed in karma; his mind was at ease and leisurely, and he once said:
idiomatic: Deeply believing in karma, at ease and leisurely, he once said:

literal: To shake out one's robes and lift one's skirt—no net of the state that swallows boats;
idiomatic: Shake out robes and lift skirts—no state net that swallows boats;

literal: to hang up one's cap and suspend one's tally—lest my will has not yet followed.
idiomatic: hang cap and tally—lest my will not yet be followed.

literal: If I might obtain Zhan Yi's release, there would be the fine advance of Ciming.
idiomatic: If I might gain Zhan Yi's release, there would be Ciming's fine advance.

literal: If I were favored with the northern old man's release, it would truly surpass the expedition against Ji'nan.
idiomatic: The northern old man's release would truly surpass Ji'nan's expedition.

literal: What is the reason?
idiomatic: What is the reason?

literal: In lanes and hamlets there is the beauty of ease; at court there is the burden of sash and cap—this has been so from of old.
idiomatic: Hamlets have ease; courts have sash and cap—so from of old.

literal: Marquis Liu followed in the tracks of Master Pine; Tao Zhu mastered the art in Xin Wen—truly there was cause.
idiomatic: Marquis Liu followed Master Pine; Tao Zhu mastered Xin Wen—there was cause.

literal: How much more when wisdom does not surpass the crowd and conduct does not tower over things, yet one wishes to toil bitterly all one's life—how eccentric!
idiomatic: When wisdom and conduct are ordinary, to toil all one's life—how eccentric!

literal: How much better to know sufficiency and stop, carefree and without burden.
idiomatic: Better to know sufficiency, carefree and unburdened.

literal: North of the northern mountain, abandoning the human world;
idiomatic: North of the northern mountain, abandon the world;

literal: south of the southern mountain, crossing beyond the world's net.
idiomatic: south of the southern mountain, cross beyond the world's net.

literal: Facing the long plain and girded by flowing water, leaning on the suburban fields and resting on the level height.
idiomatic: Face the long plain girded by water, lean on suburbs and rest on the level height.
